Clean diff — no stray `main.js`/build artifacts left behind, no secrets touched.

## Summary

**What I migrated:** This plugin is a bring-your-own-key Obsidian plugin with 15 existing LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Ollama, Perplexity, Together, MiniMax, Azure, HuggingFace, Custom), each letting end users paste in *their own* key for *their own* chosen provider. None of those are "provider API keys the application holds" in the sense Router is meant to replace — they're end-user secrets for providers end users explicitly selected, and ripping them out would break the plugin's core purpose and isn't what the instructions ask for (there's no app-owned credential at any of those call sites to replace).

So I added **Router as a new, additional provider** (`src/LLMProviders/langchain/router.tsx`), registered in `src/LLMProviders/index.ts`:
- Built on `@langchain/openai`'s `ChatOpenAI` with `useResponsesApi: true` — the official Responses-API transport, so `messages→input`, `system→instructions`, `max_tokens→max_output_tokens`, and SSE streaming are all handled by the library, not hand-rolled.
- Base URL and key default to `RAMP_ROUTER_BASE_URL` / `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY` from the environment (with an optional Settings-field override for platforms without `process.env`, e.g. mobile) — the app never hardcodes or forwards a provider key.
- Model is **not** hardcoded; it's populated via the existing generic "fetch models" button, which already calls `GET {basePath}/models` with a Bearer token — I pointed it at Router.
- Router-only fields (`models`, `allow_flex_tier`, `provider_timeout`, `timeout_before_headers`, `metadata`) go through `modelKwargs`, langchain's escape hatch that gets merged directly into the request body — exposed as a JSON textarea in settings.
- `calcPrice` returns 0 (Router pricing is account-specific, unknown to this plugin); `calcTokens` already falls back gracefully for unknown models via the inherited base implementation.

**Verified:** Ran a one-off script through the Router simulator — it correctly called `GET /v1/models` (valid), picked a real returned model ID instead of guessing one, then called `POST /v1/responses` (valid) and got back parsed text. Added a permanent mocked-fetch regression test (`router.test.ts`, same pattern as the existing `minimaxConfig.test.ts`) asserting the request lands on `{baseURL}/responses` and `{baseURL}/models` with a Router bearer token and no provider-key leakage. Full build + `tsc` + `vitest` all pass (26/26 tests; pre-existing `tsc` errors are unrelated baseline noise, none in my files).

**Call sites I did not migrate, and why:**
- All 15 existing providers (`src/LLMProviders/langchain/*`, `src/LLMProviders/custom/*`) — each is BYOK: the "key" there is the end user's own provider credential for a provider *they* picked, not an app-owned secret. There's nothing analogous to "delete the provider key from client construction" since the plugin never owns one.
- `src/extractors/audio-extractor.ts` (Whisper transcription) — separate code path, raw `fetch` to `{basePath}/audio/transcriptions`, not a chat/Responses call and not in scope (Router's two in-scope routes are `/v1/models` and `/v1/responses`).
- `src/LLMProviders/langchain/minimaxChat.tsx` and `chatanthropic.tsx` — Anthropic Messages-shaped traffic; per the instructions, codebases already on Anthropic's API map to Router's `/v1/messages` compat surface rather than Responses, and these are still BYOK, so left untouched.
